ops.new_text: \rev{The representation fed to a clustering algorithm may decide more of the outcome of clustering the electrocardiogram (ECG) than the algorithm itself. Clustering serves the clinical questions that come without labels: which patients group together, what subtypes exist, and whether structure can be found where labels are expensive or unavailable. Clustering the records directly is the natural first attempt at such questions. A clustering algorithm sees only the distances that the representation defines, however. A representation whose dominant variation is unrelated to the classes leaves every algorithm without a class signal, while one built from the quantities that define the classes may let a standard algorithm recover them. This study therefore compares representations on the same clustering algorithms, under evaluation that corrects for chance.}

ops.rationale: Opens with the point (misleading numbers, correct conclusion), uses record for one ECG, defines purity and silhouette at first use, names the project's report as the source in words, cuts simply and the self-assessment honest.
ops.new_text: \rev{A master's project that clustered whole 12-lead records reported misleading numbers, and its conclusion is the starting point of this study. The project flattened each record into a long vector, compressed it with a dense autoencoder, and clustered the code. Its report gave a high cluster purity, the share of the majority class inside the clusters, and a silhouette score near 0.89, an index of cluster compactness computed without labels. The purity equalled the majority-class proportion in every setting, however, and the silhouette was measured on a degenerate solution in which almost all points fell into a single cluster. The project concluded that the difficulty lies in processing the raw signal rather than in the clustering step. That conclusion is correct, and we make it precise.}

ops.rationale: Joins the 72-word paragraph on the closest benchmark to this paragraph on the unmeasured gap, and replaces the self-assessment and the unsupported default and canonical with what the paper shows.
ops.new_text:
A representation can carry information about a label and still fail to cluster by it.
Linear separability and clusterability are distinct properties: a representation may
place the discriminative direction far from its dominant axes of variation, so that a
supervised probe recovers the label while an unsupervised partition does not. This
distinction is established in the self-supervised learning literature
\cite{sslclustering2025}, and we treat it as background rather than as a finding. What
has not been measured, for ECG, is how the common representation families compare on
this axis under proper chance-corrected metrics.
The most directly related work benchmarks several ECG foundation models against one
another, including a cluster-separability analysis on PTB-XL \cite{lookingbeyond2026}.
By its own statement it does not include a representation-wise comparison against
hand-crafted features, and it omits the MIT-BIH database. \rev{A comparison with hand-crafted features matters because they are interpretable and need no training, and MIT-BIH adds a beat-morphology task to the rhythm task of PTB-XL.}

ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Unsupervised ECG and representations.} Hand-crafted features built from
RR-interval irregularity and beat morphology encode the defining signatures of common
arrhythmias and underpin decades of automatic analysis \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}.
Tensor and wavelet decompositions have been combined with spectral clustering for
unsupervised 12-lead classification \cite{wavelettensorecg2018}. \rev{Reconstruction autoencoders are trained to reproduce the signal, an objective that rewards signal energy and does not ask the bottleneck to separate classes, so such a bottleneck may encode a class without arranging it into clusters.} Contrastive self-supervised
methods built on physiologically motivated augmentations and patient- or lead-level
invariances, including CLOCS \cite{clocs2021}, 3KG \cite{threekg2021}, and contrastive
predictive coding for 12-lead ECG \cite{mehari2022ssl}, established the pretraining
recipes that later foundation models scaled up. Self-supervised and foundation models for
ECG, such as HuBERT-ECG \cite{hubertecg2024} and ECGFounder \cite{ecgfounder2024}, learn
general representations from millions of recordings and are now evaluated as frozen
feature extractors. \rev{The wavelet-tensor and spectral-clustering method of \cite{wavelettensorecg2018} addresses a related unsupervised goal with a different (tensor) representation. This study covers the four families above, which range from representations that encode signal energy alone, raw amplitudes and a reconstruction objective, to hand-crafted features that encode the class definition, and it leaves a tensor arm to future work.}

ops.rationale: Replaces near zero by the exact value for a one-cluster solution and the reason it follows from the definitions.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Clustering evaluation.} Cluster purity is not chance-corrected: assigning
every point to the majority class attains a purity equal to that class's prevalence.
External, chance-corrected indices, the adjusted Rand index \cite{hubertarabie1985} and
adjusted mutual information \cite{vinh2010}, \rev{are zero for a one-cluster solution, since its Rand index equals its expectation and its mutual information with the classes is zero,}
and are the appropriate headline metrics. Internal indices such as the silhouette
\cite{rousseeuw1987} measure compactness in the embedding being clustered and can be
maximised by degenerate solutions, so they require cluster-size sanity checks.

ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Closest benchmark.} \rev{The ECG foundation-model benchmark of \cite{lookingbeyond2026} reported the cluster-separability (ARI) of foundation-model embeddings on PTB-XL and found that some models clustered by clinical label while others clustered by dataset. It compared foundation models to one another and stated that prior work omits a representation-wise evaluation. It did not add a hand-crafted baseline, and it did not include MIT-BIH.} We fill both gaps and add a supervised ceiling so that
a low clustering score can be attributed to geometry rather than to missing information.

ops.new_text: \paragraph{PTB-XL.} \rev{We used PTB-XL \cite{ptbxl2020}, a public 12-lead database of 21\,799 records from 18\,869 patients. Each record holds one 10\,s signal of twelve leads, called a strip below. Rhythm labels were taken from the SCP-ECG (Standard Communications Protocol for Computer-Assisted Electrocardiography) statements. The SR-versus-AF cohort used as positives all records carrying an AF statement, AFIB (atrial fibrillation) or AFLT (atrial flutter), so atrial flutter records were counted as AF positives. Sinus-rhythm records without any AF statement served as controls.} PTB-XL encodes rhythm statements at a likelihood of zero meaning ``present'', \rev{so a presence-based rule was required, since a confidence threshold would discard every SR record. We drew a balanced, patient-disjoint cohort of 2\,542 records (1\,282 SR, 1\,260 AF), so the majority-class baseline is 0.504. Records were taken from the \mbox{100\,Hz} release of the database as signals of 1000 samples by 12 leads. No filtering, resampling or rescaling was applied before each representation's own preprocessing, so every representation started from the same signal. The lead set was chosen per representation and is stated with each representation below. All evaluation was patient-grouped: no patient appeared in more than one fold or in both classes.}

ops.rationale: Extends the 63-word paragraph with what the record grouping does and why the morphology task is a contrast to the rhythm task, in the past tense.
ops.new_text: \paragraph{MIT-BIH.} \rev{For generalization we used the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database \cite{mitbih2001,physionet2000}. Each annotated beat was segmented into a window of $[-300, +250]$\,ms around the R-peak across both leads. We formed a balanced normal-versus-premature-ventricular (N-vs-V) task of 3\,000 beats (1\,500 per class) from 47 records, with the record as the grouping unit, so that the beats of one record never fell in two folds. This is a morphology task and a deliberate contrast to the PTB-XL rhythm task. In PTB-XL the two classes differ in the rhythm of a 10\,s strip, whereas in MIT-BIH they differ in the shape of a single beat. The second task therefore tests whether the ordering of the representations depends on the kind of class difference.}

ops.new_text: \rev{HDBSCAN labels records it does not assign to any dense region as noise, and the metrics treated that label in two ways. ARI, AMI, NMI, V-measure and Fowlkes-Mallows received the prediction unchanged, so the noise records formed one further group of their own and were charged against the agreement with the true partition. Purity and the silhouette were computed on the assigned records only, because neither is defined for a set that is not a cluster, and the purity denominator stayed the full cohort. Noise records were never dropped from the evaluation and never reassigned to a nearest cluster. This treatment is why HDBSCAN sat at the bottom for every representation. At this minimum cluster size it assigned a minority of the cohort on the representations that cluster well, and on the raw, conv-AE and HuBERT-ECG matrices it labelled the entire cohort as noise, which leaves one group and an ARI of exactly zero.}

ops.new_text:
\rev{Uncertainty was quantified at two levels, which answer different questions. A percentile bootstrap over the ten per-seed values, \mbox{10\,000} resamples, measures how far a result moves when only the random seed moves. These intervals were narrow: across the five PTB-XL representations the $k$-means seed interval spanned less than 0.002 in ARI, and for two of them it had zero width because every seed returned the same partition. Ward agglomerative clustering and HDBSCAN have no seed interval at all, since each was fitted once. A seed interval therefore carries no more information than the seed standard deviation it would replace.}

\rev{The interval reported with the results is the second one, the patient-bootstrap interval: a patient-grouped percentile bootstrap over the evaluation cohort with \mbox{5\,000} resamples. The partitions were held fixed and the cohort was resampled with replacement at the patient level, so every record of a drawn patient travelled with it. Because the clustering was not refitted on each resample, the patient-bootstrap interval leaves out the variation that refitting the clusterer on a resampled cohort would add. The statistic resampled is the quantity the tables report, the mean ARI over the ten seeds where the clusterer is seeded and the single fit where it is not, so each interval contains its own point estimate. All intervals are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the bootstrap distribution at a fixed bootstrap seed.}

ops.new_text: \rev{Each paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test was reported with two effect sizes. With ten paired seeds the two-sided p-value is pinned at its floor of 0.002 as soon as every seed moves the same way, so it separates none of the contrasts and cannot express a magnitude. Cliff's delta gives the dominance of one arm over the other across all cross-seed pairs, on a scale from $-1$ to $1$, and the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation rescales the signed-rank statistic itself onto the same scale. Each headline contrast also carried the paired difference in ARI with its own paired patient-bootstrap interval.}

ops.rationale: Drops the repeated no-new-method disclaimer and its semicolon, uses feature scaling, acknowledges that the pooled scaling statistics would not be shared by separate sites, states a federated run as the procedure, past tense.
ops.new_text: \rev{To probe deployment under data siloing we used standard federated $k$-means with FedAvg-style centroid aggregation \cite{fedavg2017}. The 2\,542 records were partitioned, patient-grouped, across ten simulated sites, either independently and identically distributed (IID) or with class proportions drawn from a Dirichlet distribution so that sites differed sharply in arrhythmia prevalence (non-IID). The Dirichlet concentration was 0.3, applied per class over the ten sites, and any site left holding fewer records than clusters was dropped. Feature scaling was fitted once on the full representation matrix before partitioning, so the federation concerned the clustering step alone. Separate sites would not share these pooled statistics, a limitation taken up in Section~\ref{sec:limitations}. Federated clustering consisted of fifteen aggregation rounds of three local Lloyd iterations per site. In each round the server replaced each centroid by the mean of the site centroids, weighted by the number of records each site assigned to it, and the centroids were initialised globally from two randomly drawn records. Both settings were repeated over ten seeds, with the site partition and the centroid initialisation redrawn at each seed. We report the global ARI relative to centralized clustering of the same representation.}

ops.new_text: \rev{On PTB-XL the spread of ARI across representations was larger than the spread across clustering algorithms within a strong representation, so the representation decided the outcome (Table~\ref{tab:main} and Fig.~\ref{fig:heatmap}). ECGFounder clustered best (ARI up to 0.885 with $k$-means), the hand-crafted features were competitive (0.711 with agglomerative clustering), HuBERT-ECG was weak (0.195), and the raw and conv-AE representations were indistinguishable from a majority-class assignment (ARI $\approx 0$). Among the clusterers, HDBSCAN labelled most points as noise and underperformed throughout. Spectral clustering fell on some representations, such as HuBERT-ECG, possibly because the nearest-neighbour affinity graph was poorly connected there. The connectivity of the graph was not measured. Both clusterers are reported with the settings given in Section~\ref{sec:methods}, and their parameters were not adjusted to the outcome.}

\rev{The patient-bootstrap intervals in the caption of Table~\ref{tab:main} separated every pair of representations except raw-flatten from conv-AE, whereas moving only the seed left the $k$-means partitions almost unchanged. A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the $k$-means seeds confirmed every adjacent contrast at $p = 0.002$, the floor for ten paired samples (Section~\ref{sec:methods}). ECGFounder led the hand-crafted features by $\Delta = 0.242$ (paired patient-bootstrap interval [0.202, 0.280]), the hand-crafted features led HuBERT-ECG by $\Delta = 0.470$ ([0.424, 0.515]), and HuBERT-ECG led raw flattening by $\Delta = 0.174$ ([0.146, 0.203]). Cliff's delta and the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation were both 1.00 on all three contrasts: every cross-seed pair and every signed rank favoured the representation placed higher in the ordering. The magnitudes are therefore read from the paired differences and their intervals.}

\rev{The ordering did not depend on fixing the cluster count to the number of classes. With adjusted mutual information for $K$ from 2 to 8, ECGFounder led at every $K$, from 0.825 at $K=2$ to a minimum of 0.441 at $K=7$ and 0.450 at $K=8$. The hand-crafted features fell monotonically from 0.557 to 0.329, HuBERT-ECG stayed at or below 0.132, and the raw representation never exceeded 0.005. HuBERT-ECG and raw flattening thus stayed low at every cluster count, so their low ARI at two clusters is not an effect of the chosen $K$.}

ops.new_text:
\rev{The position of each representation followed from two things: how much of the label its space holds, which the supervised ceiling in the last column of Table~\ref{tab:main} measures, and where in the space that label lies. The hand-crafted representation is 16-dimensional and each coordinate is a quantity by which the classes are defined, RR irregularity and P-wave presence. Its ceiling was 0.942 and an unsupervised partition recovered 0.711. ECGFounder had the highest ceiling, 0.983, recovered the most, 0.885, and led at every $K$ from 2 to 8, so the rhythm split is one of the larger sources of variation in its 1024 dimensions. HuBERT-ECG had almost the same ceiling as the hand-crafted features, 0.899, and recovered 0.195. The two foundation models thus did not behave as one category, which matches the report of \cite{lookingbeyond2026} that some ECG foundation embeddings organise by clinical label and others by dataset.}

\rev{The raw and conv-AE representations both sat at a majority-class assignment under all five clusterers, for different reasons. The conv-AE ceiling of 0.678 is what a bottleneck optimised to reconstruct signal energy retains of a class it was never asked about, and it recovered 0.008. Raw flattening reached a ceiling of 0.519 against a majority of 0.504, so a linear probe found almost no label in the 1992-dimensional vector. Its coordinates are amplitudes at fixed sample offsets, and a likely cause of this linear failure is that no fixed offset falls on the same part of the cardiac cycle in two records. A random forest on the same vector reached 0.714, so the misalignment limits what a linear readout can find. The raw representation therefore lacks linearly recoverable label information, while the conv-AE holds label information without arranging it into clusters, and changing the clustering algorithm addresses neither.}

ops.new_text: \subsection[Supervised separability and clustering]{\rev{Supervised separability and clustering}}

ops.rationale: Limits the raw claim to linearly recoverable information, names the conv-AE, cuts simply and both semicolons, splits off the non-linear probe check and adds what the hand-crafted and ECGFounder probe values mean for the claim, past tense.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The supervised ceilings (last column of Table~\ref{tab:main} and Fig.~\ref{fig:sep}) exposed a gap between separability and clusterability. The raw representation carried almost no linearly recoverable label information (ceiling 0.519, barely above the 0.504 majority), consistent with its chance-level clustering. The conv-AE was more separable (0.678) yet still clustered at chance (best ARI 0.008, from Ward agglomerative clustering), so the conv-AE encoded the class without organising it into clusters. HuBERT-ECG was the sharpest case, with a ceiling of 0.899 but an ARI of only 0.195. ECGFounder and the hand-crafted features achieved both high separability and high clusterability. In the weaker embeddings the discriminative information exists but does not lie along their dominant axes of variation, the established separability-versus-clusterability effect \cite{sslclustering2025}.}

\rev{A non-linear probe showed that this gap is not an artefact of a linear probe. A random forest on the raw features reached accuracy 0.714, well above its linear ceiling of 0.519 and far above its clustering ARI of 0.000, so even a non-linear decoder recovered a label that clustering did not. The same probe gave 0.951 on the hand-crafted features, 0.983 on ECGFounder and 0.825 on HuBERT-ECG. On ECGFounder the two probes agreed to three decimals, the linear ceiling at 0.9831 and the random forest at 0.9835. On the two representations that cluster well the non-linear probe therefore added little over the linear ceiling (0.951 against 0.942 for the hand-crafted features), so their clustering is not held back by information that only a non-linear readout reaches. For HuBERT-ECG the random forest sat below the linear ceiling of 0.899, so probe linearity does not account for that gap either.}

ops.rationale: Opens by naming the reading the out-of-fold test checks, splits the procedure and values from their interpretation, removes both semicolons, past tense.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The reading that the class information of the weaker embeddings lies off their dominant axes was tested out of fold. If it holds, a single direction estimated from other patients should recover the class. A linear discriminant was fitted on the training patients of a patient-grouped stratified five-fold split, the held-out patients were projected onto that single axis, and the projection was clustered with $k$-means without labels. The comparison arm was $k$-means on the same held-out records in their native representation. Fitting the discriminant on every label and then clustering the projection would recover the labels by construction, which is why the projected patients were held out. Over five folds and ten seeds, on 508 or 509 held-out records per fold, the mean ARI rose from 0.160 to 0.549 for HuBERT-ECG, from 0.003 to 0.121 for the conv-AE, from 0.646 to 0.758 for the hand-crafted features and from 0.893 to 0.923 for ECGFounder. It did not move for raw flattening, 0.000 to 0.001. These are held-out values, so the native column does not equal the full-cohort $k$-means ARIs of Table~\ref{tab:main}. The largest difference is 0.013, on HuBERT-ECG.}

\rev{HuBERT-ECG showed the largest gain. One direction estimated from other patients recovered more than three times what its own 768 dimensions yield unsupervised, so the class information is present, transfers across patients, and lies away from the directions that dominate the embedding. ECGFounder gained almost nothing, because its dominant axes already carry the split. The conv-AE rose off chance and stopped far short of its ceiling of 0.678, so its class structure is both off-axis and diffuse. Raw flattening did not move at all, which separates its failure from that of HuBERT-ECG. No single direction estimated from other patients separates the classes in it, and whatever the non-linear probe recovers from it is not of that form.}

ops.new_text: \rev{Internal indices misled here in a specific, reproducible way. Raw flattening with agglomerative clustering attained a silhouette of 0.81 while its largest cluster held a fraction of 1.00 of the cohort and the ARI was 0.000. The hand-crafted representation, which recovered the classes (ARI 0.711, balanced clusters), had a \emph{lower} silhouette of 0.28 (Fig.~\ref{fig:trap}). A degenerate one-cluster solution maximises compactness while carrying no class information. This is the artefact behind the original project's silhouette of 0.89, and it is why chance-corrected external metrics, read together with cluster-size sanity checks, are necessary.}

ops.new_text: \rev{The mean ARI over clusterers depended on the feature scaling. For the hand-crafted features it was 0.629 under standard scaling and 0.606 under power scaling, but fell to 0.360 under robust scaling and 0.229 under quantile scaling. The effect was not confined to the hand-crafted features: the mean ARI of ECGFounder dropped from 0.866 under standard scaling to 0.093 under robust scaling. Robust scaling leaves heavy arrhythmic tails unbounded, so a few outliers may dominate Euclidean distance and collapse the partition. Feature scaling should therefore be reported in ECG clustering, together with a sweep over scaling methods.}

ops.new_text: \rev{The ordering of the representations replicated on a different dataset and a different task type (Table~\ref{tab:mitbih}). On the N-vs-V beat-morphology task the 21-dimensional beat-morphology feature set clustered well (ARI 0.783), whereas the raw beat window did not (ARI 0.018 with $k$-means and 0.049 with agglomerative clustering), although the beats were R-peak aligned. The conv-AE was again the clean separability-versus-clusterability case, with a supervised ceiling of 0.927 but a best ARI of only 0.127, from the Gaussian mixture. The same pattern appeared for rhythm on PTB-XL and for morphology on MIT-BIH, which supports the representation-level reading of the PTB-XL results.}

ops.new_text: \rev{The two stressors changed the comparison in different ways. Under class imbalance the hand-crafted features overtook ECGFounder, and under non-IID federation the two means came closer while their spread over the site draws differed. At the natural-like 9:1 SR:AF ratio (majority 0.90) the ARI of every representation above chance fell, possibly in part because a 10\% minority cluster is hard to isolate with a partitional method. The hand-crafted features retained the most structure over the ten seeds (ARI 0.265 [0.250, 0.280], AMI 0.245 [0.233, 0.257]) and \emph{overtook} ECGFounder (ARI 0.063 [0.061, 0.065], AMI 0.148 [0.143, 0.152]), with no overlap between the two ARI intervals. HuBERT-ECG reached an ARI similar to that of ECGFounder (0.061 [0.053, 0.069]) at a lower AMI (0.044 [0.037, 0.050]). Its partition thus agreed with the classes on record pairs about as well as that of ECGFounder, beyond chance, but carried less information about them. The raw and conv-AE representations stayed at chance (0.000 and 0.004). The reversal was observed at this one ratio and under power scaling, and it is a result for that setting.}

ops.rationale: Opens with the non-IID result limited to the representations above chance, joins the label fragment, uses sites, states ECGFounder's ARI rather than its advantage, the measured retention in place of most robust, the worst site draw as this study's stated criterion with its reason, the seed interval named apart from the patient-bootstrap interval, the restating and unhedged close cut and scoped to the simulation, past tense.
ops.new_text: \rev{Non-IID site heterogeneity reduced the ARI of every representation whose centralized ARI is above zero, and it did so unequally. Under IID federation across ten sites every representation retained essentially its centralized ARI, which validates the federated procedure (Table~\ref{tab:fed} and Fig.~\ref{fig:fed}). Under non-IID federation the hand-crafted features retained 92\% of their centralized ARI (0.644 to 0.591), while the ARI of ECGFounder fell from 0.885 to 0.612. The two means were close, 0.612 against 0.591, and they did not carry the same risk. Across the ten redrawn site partitions the seed bootstrap interval of the hand-crafted features was [0.546, 0.631] and their worst single partition still returned 0.455. The interval of ECGFounder was [0.382, 0.796], and three of its ten partitions fell to 0.132 or below, one of them to chance. This study takes the worst site draw as its deployment criterion, because a deployment meets a single site partition, and the mean over ten draws does not show how low that partition can fall. On that criterion the hand-crafted features retained more of their clustering ARI than ECGFounder under simulated site heterogeneity on PTB-XL.}

ops.new_text: \rev{Table~\ref{tab:cost} gives the cost of computing each representation, which bears on deployment alongside the ARI. ECGFounder, which clustered best, was the most expensive per record, at fifteen times the hand-crafted extraction. Both foundation models needed a gigabyte or more of resident memory against \mbox{364\,MB} for the hand-crafted features, about a third of the memory of ECGFounder, and the hand-crafted features carry no learned parameters at all. Clustering itself was negligible everywhere, under \mbox{0.3\,s} for the whole cohort at any of the five dimensionalities, so the cost of a representation is the cost of extracting it.}

ops.new_text:
\rev{The foundation-model axis is bounded to two models by selection rather than by survey.
HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder both publish weights that load into a frozen feature extractor
without fine-tuning, which is what a benchmark of frozen embeddings requires, and they differ
in pretraining objective and architecture, a self-supervised transformer
\cite{hubertecg2024} against a convolutional model pretrained on more than ten million
recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}. Their clustering ARIs are also far apart, 0.885 against 0.195, so the foundation arm is not a single point. What the
bound does to the conclusions is to scope them: every statement here about a foundation model
is a statement about one of these two, the deployment comparison is between the hand-crafted
features and ECGFounder specifically, and none of it extends to ECG foundation models as a
class. A further model that clusters as well as ECGFounder on balanced data would leave the
results reported here unchanged, and would have to be measured again under imbalance and
under federation before the deployment reading could be extended to it.}

ops.new_text: \rev{For unsupervised arrhythmia structure in the ECG, the choice of representation moved clustering ARI further than the choice of clustering algorithm on the two tasks evaluated, and chance-corrected external evaluation was required to see it. On balanced PTB-XL data ECGFounder, pretrained on more than ten million recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}, leads. Under class imbalance 16 interpretable hand-crafted features overtake it. Under simulated federation across ten heterogeneous sites they retain 0.92 of their centralized ARI against 0.69 and never fall below 0.455 over the ten site draws. On PTB-XL the raw and conv-AE representations sit at chance under all five clusterers. Internal indices and feature scaling are not neutral choices and must be reported. Whether these results hold for multi-class arrhythmia cohorts, for other foundation models and for a real multi-institution federation is open.}
